- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.33), model tends to over-forecast; adjust downward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- Model consistently under-responds to recent price spikes; if last 3–5 prices are rising, add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast.
- Model over-anticipates mean reversion after sharp moves; if recent sentiment is neutral or mixed, reduce forecast slope to avoid overshoot.
- For 30-day horizon, model often lags by 1–3 days; if sentiment is trending, shift forecast 1–2 days ahead with slight upward bias.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to misalign with cycle peak; align forecast with sentiment momentum rather than historical mean.
